sourceReview.learningGoal: Show why a sliding window turns nested-loop subarray work into a linear pass.
sourceReview.caveat: Complexity depends on the exact problem constraints; this reel uses a fixed-size window sum as the teaching example.

claims.claim: A fixed-size sliding window can compute each next subarray sum in O(1) after the first window, for O(n) overall.

beats.headline:
Nested loops
kill speed.
beats.subhead: Subarray sums with two loops become O(n²).
beats.narration: Nested loops make your code crawl. What if you could slide a window and turn O(n²) subarray work into O(n)?

beats.headline:
Every window
recounted.
beats.subhead: Nested loops recompute the same cells again.
beats.narration: Whenever you need contiguous subarray sums, nested loops recount the same cells again and again — and that becomes O(n²).

beats.headline:
Fix the size.
Slide the frame.
beats.subhead: A fixed-length window does not need a full rescan.
beats.narration: But if the window size is fixed, you do not need to rescan every cell. That pattern is the sliding window technique.

beats.headline:
Minus left.
Plus right.
beats.subhead: Reuse the previous sum — O(1) per slide.
beats.narration: As the window slides, subtract the element leaving on the left and add the new one on the right. No full recount — O(1) per move.

beats.headline:
One pass.
Not n² passes.
beats.subhead: Sliding window scans the array once — O(n).
beats.narration: That is the payoff: nested loops cost O(n²), while a sliding window scans the array once — O(n).

beats.headline:
Left and right
hold the window.
beats.subhead: Grow with right, shrink with left.
beats.narration: Two pointers hold the window — left and right. Grow with right when the condition fits; shrink with left when it breaks.

beats.headline:
Interview signal:
sliding window.
beats.narration: In interviews, max-sum subarray or longest substring questions are a signal — sliding window is your O(n) weapon.

beats.headline:
Next up:
two pointers.
beats.narration: Next up: two pointers — solve array problems even faster.
